agent_note: Prose fiction (retold myth), not verse. Two clearly separable layers. (1) The tales are narrated retrospectively in past tense -- 11 of 15 event quotes, all third-person past scene narration of Thor, Loki, Odin. (2) A present-tense expository layer describes the world and its cosmology atemporally (q01684 Loki, q01700 Gjallerhorn/Ragnarok, q01701 Ratatosk and the world-tree, q01692 the summation of how the worlds end). That is a frame/register, not simultaneous narration, which is why narrating_situation is retrospective despite 26.7% present. A further four quotes are the author's first-person introduction and are discarded as paratext -- an unusually heavy paratext leak because Goodreads treats the introduction as part of the work. Expect SPLIT_REVIEW at 11 past / 4 present; the cause is 'mixed -- strand' (expository frame). FLIP LEVER: the four present quotes are all cosmological exposition. If a reader files them as front-matter/glossary paratext or as gnomic, the book becomes 11 past / 0 present and lands HIGH CONF PAST. q01684 is the most vulnerable -- it reads like a dramatis-personae entry.
